memories.content:
Prevention layer (agentic-research-lab, 2026-09-30) built against the deleted-evidence failure: (1) PreToolUse hook scripts/hook_guard_evidence.py denies rm/rmdir/Remove-Item/truncate/glob against reflection/digests|candidates|.snapshots — verified against the actual fatal command; writes still allowed because the agent must produce these files. (2) scripts/snapshot_graded.py copies graded artifacts to reflection/.snapshots/<ts>/ before every check_reflection read; recovery proven by deleting and restoring an artifact. (3) check_reflection.py --paths <slug> grades only the named run's artifacts (a directory-wide gate cannot distinguish "my change is broken" from "old artifact is broken"). (4) preflight.py consumes reflection/logs/*.status.json: failed/timeout/error and dead-PID running block; a stale failure whose artifacts now re-grade clean is reported ok instead of blocking forever (blocking forever creates pressure to delete the evidence the check preserves). (5) docs/CODING_STANDARDS.md as reviewer-loaded file. (6) check_slop.py skips bg-smoke* test fixtures — smoke-test prose is not research output, but check_reflection still grades those files fully.

Four plan items deliberately NOT built: icacls read-only freeze (locks inside the worker cannot intercept the agent's own Bash tool — the actual deletion vector — so the PreToolUse hook is the real boundary; also ACL denials leave un-removable files that wedge the pipeline); shell-confirmation tokens for rm -rf (not enforceable by a rule, the hook denies outright instead); three-context implementer/reviewer/verifier orchestration (half-day, needs pi task/session primitives, and check_evidence_guard.py already enforces the invariant deterministically without new roles); model tier routing (no router config surface in this workspace).

memories.content:
pi token efficiency (2026-09-30, workspace root_worksapce): measured over 29 sessions / 69.5M tokens. Cache hit ratio 78.0%. Cold-prefix attribution (a turn with cacheRead==0 and input>2000) gave: non-caching provider 61.2% of wasted tokens (oc/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free = 4.0M tok, 0.0% hit ratio), thinking_level_change 12.5% (812K), model_switch 7.7% (502K), compaction 5.6%, context_edit 3.1%. Decisive finding: caching is a property of the model, not the task — one model held 90.3% for 363 consecutive turns. Tool output was 11.7x assistant output chars (1.71M vs 146K), the biggest untapped lever.

DECISION D15: one model per session, never switch mid-session; roles are thinking modes not routing targets. User rejected architect/editor model delegation because model availability is not stable for them.

Tooling scars: (1) cacheWrite is 0 in every pi session — this provider tier has no write-side accounting, so cold prefixes are invisible in cost data; detect via cacheRead==0, never via cost. (2) A wrong attribution looks authoritative — attributing cold prefixes to the nearest preceding event blamed thinking_change for 67.9% of waste when a 0.0%-hit-ratio provider was the real cause. Verify attribution against per-model ratios within one session before acting.

Scripts (stdlib only): scripts/pi_token_audit.py, pi_context_growth.py, pi_cache_forensics.py. Evidence in root TOKEN-EFFICIENCY.md. Note: root has NO docs/ directory convention — knowledge lives as root files (PHILOSOPHY.md, TOOLS.md); check_workspace_integrity.py enforces ALLOWED_ROOT, so a new root file must be declared there.

memories.content:
jCodeMunch MCP (2026-09-30, root_worksapce) — DECISION D16: wired in with pi codemode exposure. Real project: github.com/jgravelle/jcodemunch-mcp, 2,721 stars, 365 forks, Python + tree-sitter, v1.108.319 via `uv tool install` (NOT npm — no npm/pypi package exists). Config in ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json as `jcodemunch`, exposure codemode, only menu/route/set_tool_tier declared to the model; announce_model + jcodemunch_guide hidden.

Verified claims: get_symbol_source returned 1,300 chars for a symbol whose file is 7,669 chars = 5.9x. search_symbols 629 chars. find_importers + get_call_hierarchy work (grep cannot do these).

The 90-tool objection does NOT hold: pi's codemode exposure means MCP schemas never enter the system prefix at all. Separately, jcodemunch's own docs say the schema block is paid ~once per cache lifetime then at cache-read rates — reading it as a per-request saving overstates cost ~10x. Its 'counter' surface shows only 6 of 94 tools.

THE REAL CEILING (measured with scripts/tool_output_breakdown.py on own transcripts): tool output = bash 59.4%, read 27.1%, codemode 6.3%, powershell 5.2%. Source-file reads are only 12.1% of ALL tool output. So symbol retrieval addresses ~12%, saving ~8.5% at a 70% cut. The vendor's 96.5% / 28.3x is a per-read figure, not a share-of-context figure — roughly an order of magnitude overstatement. bash/test/git output is the bigger unaddressed fish.

Operational gotchas: repo resolution is by git remote name (kamyczeczek/agentic-research-lab), not folder path. CLI needs absolute paths, relative rejected. get_symbol_source needs file::name#kind symbol_id, not path+symbol. menu costs 5,139 chars so it's discovery-only, not per-symbol. No enforcement hooks installed: they rewrite global CLAUDE.md + client settings, pi has no such hook surface, and it conflicts with the workspace 'config != working config' rule.

New scripts: scripts/mcp_schema_cost.py (measures any MCP server's tool-surface prefix cost), scripts/mcp_call.py (call one MCP tool, print payload size), scripts/tool_output_breakdown.py. jDocMunch deferred — doc reads are 12.1% and mostly small files.
